bugs.title: Replace color grade/LUT with new look derived from 960x540 8x8 gradient-tile reference image (vibrant, high-saturation, multi-hue) — build a real grade, do NOT apply image as HALD CLUT
bugs.notes: FINDINGS: the grade lived in pipeline/stage_b/enhance.py — haldclut=shortest=1 against assets/anime_reference_color_cube_l8.png (a 64^3 Hald L8 PNG converted from assets/anime_reference_lut_grid.png), inserted between hqdn3d denoise and the bug-11 2x lanczos upscale, with bug-25 rescale-back and cas/unsharp sharpening AFTER the grade. The user-supplied 960x540 8x8 gradient-tile reference is NOT a valid HALD CLUT identity (HALD must be perfect-square, e.g. 512x512, encoding every RGB input in deterministic layout), so it was treated strictly as a mood reference and never fed to haldclut. FIX: new pipeline/stage_b/build_glow_lut.py synthesises a real 64^3 3D LUT encoding the reference's character — warm S-curve contrast (+whisper of shadow lift), ~1.5x vibrance saturation boost (power<1 so low-sat pixels lift more), and a +18deg hue rotation gated by ORIGINAL saturation (smoothstep 0.25..0.75) so neutrals/shadows/speculars keep their hue — and writes assets/vibrant_glow_color_cube_l8.png (Hald L8) + vibrant_glow_grade.cube. common.py now points LUT_GRID_SOURCE/LUT_HALD_ASSET at the new assets; enhance.py docstring updated. Denoise/upscale/cas/unsharp/rescale/deband order preserved verbatim (grade still before sharpening). VERIFICATION: LUT table entries sampled (pure red->orange 255,77,0; mid grey shifts warm; dark greys stay neutral). Real render: 3s testsrc2+audio clip run through the ACTUAL enhance_one() chain — output validates mobile-safe (540x300 yuv420p 30/1 CFR High@L4.0), and frame analysis confirms the look: saturated-pixel mean saturation 0.988->0.993 and hue histogram mass visibly rotated (red bin -> yellow bin, +18deg). NOTE: the 960x540 reference image itself was never committed to the repo, so the grade was built from the brief's documented description of it (vibrant, high-saturation, multi-hue gradient bands); tuneables (SAT_BOOST/HUE_SHIFT_DEG/CONTRAST/WARMTH) sit at the top of build_glow_lut.py if the owner wants the look adjusted against the actual image.

bugs.title: Cosmetic UI overhaul — bot-wide animations/liveliness pass with shared animation helpers, respecting Telegram edit rate limits
bugs.notes: FINDINGS: animation code from prior sweeps was scattered — bug-35's spinner burst + progress bar (progress.js, used only at stage dispatch/restart), bug-42/44's paste-assembly indicator, and ad-hoc terminal marks (✅/⚠️/⛔) hardcoded separately in tasks.js and done.js; active-state rows had NO glyph at all. FIX: (1) new bot/src/anim.js establishes one shared design language — pulseFrames/loadingFrames/dotsBar (moving-window indeterminate bar), a canonical statusEmoji map for every job state, pulseTaskLines, toggleFeedback, saveConfirmFlash, and flashThenView — with a hard rate-limit contract: max one transient beat + one settle write per interaction, no edit loops (the bug-35 self-limiting burst is unchanged). (2) Wired bot-wide: /tasks rows carry the canonical per-state glyph (⚙️ stage A, 🎬 stage B, 📂 awaiting file, 📝 awaiting plan, 🕓 queued, ❔ unreadable — active states previously showed nothing) plus a live indeterminate 'working' hint line whenever any job is active; task detail State line leads with the same glyph; /done routes its marks through statusEmoji; settings get toggle feedback — narrator-voice select and the Series Mode toggle now flash '✅ Saved — …' before settling, and the clone sync check/apply screens show pulse+dots+moving-bar loading beats instead of a bare '…'. VERIFICATION: cannot run a live Telegram bot here (Worker + real bot token required), so no visual confirmation in a client; verified via the unit suite instead — 109/109 tests pass (node --test), including new animation.test.mjs covering every anim.js primitive and flashThenView's no-loop contract, and updated tasks.test.mjs rows. Note: 5 pre-existing test failures seen before any edits were purely missing node_modules (tweetnacl) in this sandbox — resolved with npm install, unrelated to the sweep. (commit sha recorded post-rebase: wiring=f7feccc, helpers=b3539a2)
